paper: LLMFactor: Extracting Profitable Factors through Prompts for Explainable Stock Movement Prediction
headline_mechanism: LLMFactor sequentially infers a related company, extracts the top five price-relevant factors from current news, and combines relation, factors, and five prior price movements to predict rise or fall with an explanation.

source_anchors.claim: The first prompt identifies the relationship between the target and another company mentioned in its news.
The second prompt extracts the top k factors expected to affect the target stock price.
Relation, factors, and a textual sequence of prior rose/fell movements jointly determine the next rise/fall prediction.
Both the price window and extracted factor count are fixed at five.

preserved_elements: three sequential relation, factor, and prediction stages
one related-stock feature for every target formation
selection of exactly five price-relevant factors
rolling binary rise/fall prediction trained only on earlier observations
public explanation diagnostics naming the relation and selected factors
approximated_elements: nearest fundamental/size peer replaces company-name matching in unavailable news
eight JKP attention, earnings, valuation, quality, and distress signals replace generated news factors
rolling RankICIR replaces LLM ranking of factor relevance
numeric monthly returns replace textual daily rose/fell sentences
rolling ridge classification replaces the unspecified LLM request, parser, and rationale
invented_elements: the peer-state distance and positive similar-company relation
ridge penalty and continuous classification margin
common value-weighted long/short decile portfolio adapter
portfolio_adapter: The continuous rise/fall margin is ranked within the frozen monthly top-1,000 universe and mapped to common value-weighted long/short deciles with 10 bp one-way cost.
claim_boundary: This is a researcher-authored LLMFactor-inspired numeric sequential predictor, not the unavailable news, company matcher, prompts, LLM responses, parser, rationales, daily labels, or native result tables.
